players.product: long-haul / middle-mile fiber construction for hyperscaler data-center interconnect

quarterly_data.signal: Long-haul / middle-mile data-center fiber: CEO says the $20 billion long-haul middle-mile opportunity set first cited about five quarters ago 'has certainly grown' (updated internally, not published). A customer is discussing hyperscaler routes with up to 7,500-10,000 fiber strands per route, versus the 864 or 1728 count fiber being placed today, which he calls 'a decade plus long build'. The work is 'still in early innings': programs take 'a year-ish' from announcement to start, calendar 2027 comes online and calendar 2028 is 'that fast and furious year'; Dycom believes it was 'first on the field' and keeps winning more.
quarterly_data.figure: $20 billion opportunity set (grown, not updated publicly); routes up to 7,500-10,000 fiber strands vs 864 or 1728 count fiber today; ramp calendar 2027, especially calendar 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Communications growth was driven by ramping fiber-to-the-home programs, increased long-haul and middle-mile builds and growing maintenance services; Communications adjusted EBITDA increased 28% to $192.4 million. Management says fiber-to-the-home work grew 33% sequentially in one quarter (not normally published), with ramps across many customers and markets, and the raised Communications outlook (about 12.6%-15.8% organic growth) is 'largely Fiber-to-the-Home'; long-haul/middle-mile is smaller today. Q1 was helped by weather ('behaved more like a Q2 or a Q3'), so the Q2 outlook does not show the same upswing. Management also cited Corning's announcements to scale fiber manufacturing as evidence of demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Communications adj. EBITDA $192.4 million (+28%); fiber-to-the-home work +33% quarter-over-quarter; Communications organic growth outlook 12.6%-15.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center demand and contract structure: inside-the-fence and connected middle-mile fiber continues to grow and data-center demand 'has not abated whatsoever. In fact, it's only increasing.' Customers are extending contract durations to lock up Dycom's skilled workforce through the end of the decade, with work contracted three or four years out (still mostly under MSAs or long-term agreements), and management says fuel-cost increases are modeled into the outlook. Dycom added 730 employees in the quarter (about 20,000 teammates) and passes on low-bid work.
quarterly_data.figure: 730 employees added in Q1; 20,000 teammates; contracts three or four years out

quarterly_data.signal: Building Systems (Power Solutions data-center electrical): adjusted EBITDA was $70 million, and the full-year outlook implies Power Solutions doubling its trailing 4-5 year CAGR, 'from 15% to 30% plus growth', with the margin expected in the high teens for the year, similar to Q1. The segment's contracted backlog is small because projects are contracted right before build starts, but its 'awarded but not contracted' and shadow backlog are 'multiples' of the reported backlog; next-12-month and total backlog are very close numerically.
quarterly_data.figure: Building Systems adj. EBITDA $70 million; growth from 15% to 30% plus; high-teens margin

quarterly_data.signal: National Technology Integrators (NTI) deal terms from the call: purchase price $275 million on a cash-free, debt-free basis (approximately $234 million cash plus approximately $41 million of Dycom stock), historically mid-to-high-teens adjusted EBITDA margins, expected to close in fiscal Q2 with pro forma net leverage below 2.5 times. NTI's revenue is about two-thirds data-center exposure; it works for general contractors and has hyperscaler relationships, with operations in the D.M.V., Texas and the Midwest. Management plans a combined offer of Power Solutions electrical, NTI structured cabling, Communications inside-the-fence fiber and long-haul/middle-mile routes, 'starting at the racks and connecting data centers across America'.
quarterly_data.figure: $275 million purchase price (~$234 million cash, ~$41 million stock); about two-thirds data center exposure; pro forma net leverage below 2.5 times

quarterly_data.signal: BEAD (federal broadband program) is progressing through state and subgrantee pipelines; management still expects some BEAD revenue in fiscal Q2 from smaller programs (not included in the outlook), with the program really taking hold in calendar 2027. Balance sheet: combined DSOs of 96 days (15 days better year-over-year, seen as sustainable), 100,000 shares repurchased for approximately $36 million, cash of $538.8 million, liquidity over $1.28 billion and pro forma net leverage of approximately 2.3x.
quarterly_data.figure: BEAD revenue expected in Q2 (not in outlook); DSOs 96 days; cash $538.8 million; liquidity over $1.28 billion; net leverage approximately 2.3x
